In addition, we investigated varying formaldehyde concentrations to examine the impact on FORCE pathway flux using previously identified HACS, RuHACS. Interestingly, improvement in glycolate flux with increasing formaldehyde concentrations saturated between 2.5 mM and 5 mM formaldehyde, and there was a notable drop in glycolate flux at 10 mM, possibly due to 34 the toxicity of formaldehyde. Establishing a 96 well-based resting-cell bioconversion platform and screening first-round HACS variants. (A) GA production from formaldehyde and formate via formate activation enzyme (AbfT) and HACS. A previously demonstrated pathway (Chou et al., 2019) for formaldehyde-to-GA bioconversion 35 with HACS, ACR, and ALDH are shown in light gray. (B) HACS and AbfT are expressed under independently inducible promoters: HACS expressed under the IPTG-inducible T7 promoter and AbfT under the cumate-inducible T5 promoter. (C) Bioconversion platform was scaled down from a shake flask (5–10 mL) to a 96-deep-well microtiter plate (1 mL) for improved throughput. (D) First-round HACS variants organized in a phylogenetic tree diagram with a heatmap diagram representing the GA flux. Node and subclades that branch out RuHACS, ApbHACS, and DhcHACS are highlighted in dark green. Variants highlighted in bold represent the selected variants as a reference for the second-round bioprospecting. Branches and leaves that belong to the OXC cluster are highlighted in red. MeOXC4 is an engineered version of MeOXC to have HACS activities. RuHACS was reported to exhibit both improved apparent K toward formaldehyde and M higher expression level in E. coli compared to the human enzyme (HsHACS). Using RuHACS as a reference, an unsorted gene homolog database was collected using Basic Local Alignment Search Tool (BLAST) with the E-value cutoff set based on the E- value between RuHACS and oxalyl-CoA decarboxylase (OXC) from Escherichia coli (EcOXC) and Oxalobacter formigenes (OfOXC). The CD-HIT web server was used to sort and select representative variants by clustering query results into groups with specific identity threshold. A restriction of 70% identity threshold was imposed for genes from prokaryotic origin whereas 50% was used for no taxonomic restriction. Clustering and selecting representative genes using CD-HIT identified 93 HACS variants similar to RuHACS. The list was further curated by removing sequences with lengths greater than one standard deviation from the mean and variants from Animalia, which could result in poor expression in E. coli. As a result, 34 remaining variants were chosen after curation for testing. The selected genes were codon-optimized for expression in E. coli with five variants failing during the synthesis process, which left 29 HACS variants for the first screening round (HACS-1-1 to HACS-1-29).
